Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
204 AM PST Thu Nov 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Warmer than average temperatures with increased areas of mid to
  high level cloud continue from Thanksgiving Day through 
  Saturday. 

* Dry conditions prevail through Saturday, except for a slight
  chance for light rain showers Friday night near the Oregon
  border.

* Rain and higher elevation snow return Sunday into Monday, with
  more impactful storm potential for the first week of December.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

High pressure extending into CA-NV will keep mainly dry weather 
and good holiday travel conditions through Saturday night. This 
ridge is relatively flat so areas of mid-high level clouds from
the Pacific will stream overhead for much of this time frame. 
This cloud deck becomes thicker by Friday afternoon-evening 
especially north of I-80 as a weak upper disturbance pushes across
the Pacific NW, bringing a period of increased west winds over 
Sierra ridges, with gusts up to 60 mph through Friday night. A few
light rain showers could also accompany this system north of
Susanville-Gerlach to the Oregon border Friday night, although
most scenarios bring only a trace to a few hundredths of an inch,
with only a 20-35% chance of at least 0.10" north of Cedarville.

Otherwise, despite the cloud cover and overall light winds with
valley inversions that could reduce air quality each morning,
temperatures will climb into the mid 50s-lower 60s in most areas
each day through Saturday--about 5-10 degrees above late November
averages. For those getting an early start on holiday shopping 
Friday morning, it will be a bit chilly with lows mainly in the 
mid 20s-mid 30s, then the thicker cloud cover will bring milder 
conditions for the next two nights/mornings.

The shift to a more active storm pattern is still expected to
start Sunday, although the onset for this first round of rain and
higher elevation snow (snow levels 7500-8000 ft) is trending a bit
later, with the best chances later Sunday afternoon through late
evening. Snowfall amounts aren't expected be significant with this
first storm, with only a 10-25% chance for accumulations of 2" or
more at the main pass levels. Even if the roads are only wet or
slushy, anyone traveling over the main Sierra passes as the 
holiday weekend wraps up should still allow extra time. Winds will
also pick up Sunday-Sunday night especially for Sierra ridges.

The next storm is projected to arrive by late Monday and continue
through Tuesday or Tuesday night. This storm could be more 
impactful with heavier Sierra snow and lowering snow levels to the
5500-6500 ft range. The snow amounts still show a wide range of 
outcomes, depending on the eventual storm track. Additional storms
could then follow by later next week into the first weekend of 
December, although latest ensemble guidance is trending toward a 
1-3 day break after the Monday-Tuesday storm moves through. 
Overall, plan for periods of winter conditions if planning travel
across the Sierra next week. 

MJD

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light surface winds and widespread areas of
  high level/cirrus clouds through early Friday morning. Valley
  inversions may also lead to increased haze buildup through late 
  morning, with minor reductions in slantwise visibility.

Regional Outlook: 

* FZFG with LIFR conditions for KTRK through 15-16Z this morning
  and returning tonight after 06-08Z. Otherwise, VFR conditions
  with light surface winds and widespread areas of high clouds
  through early Friday morning. Valley inversions may also lead to 
  increased haze buildup through late morning at KCXP/KMEV, with 
  minor reductions in slantwise visibility. 
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* VFR conditions with mainly light surface winds continue through
  early Sunday, except for FZFG potential (60-80% chance) with
  LIFR conditions Friday and Saturday mornings at KTRK. However,
  areas of cirrus may limit the duration and extent of this fog.
  Valley inversions may also lead to increased haze buildup mainly
  around KRNO/KCXP/KMEV each morning, with minor reductions in
  slantwise visibility. FL100 west winds increase with gusts near
  50 kt, leading to increased turbulence and periods of LLWS 
  Friday night.
